content: Drebrin is a protein in humans that is encoded by the DBN1 gene. This protein is a cytoplasmic actin-binding protein, which is believed to play a significant role in the process of neuronal growth. It belongs to the drebrin family of proteins, which are developmentally regulated in the brain. A reduction in the levels of this protein in the brain has been implicated as a potential contributing factor in the development of memory disturbances associated with Alzheimer’s disease. At least two alternative splice variants of the DBN1 gene have been identified, which encode different protein isoforms. Model organisms have been utilized to study the function of the DBN1 gene. A conditional knockout mouse line, referred to as Dbn1tm1b(KOMP)Wtsi, was created at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute. Both male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening to assess the effects of the gene deletion.
